extra.message: User-controlled 'weightFormula' (from formData, line 528) is interpolated into a Function constructor: new Function('criteria', `return (${formula});`). This allows arbitrary JavaScript code execution (remote code execution) by any user with grading permissions (instructor/TA/admin).

searchEnrollmentFeed() builds SQL via sql.raw(`enrollments.${field} = '${value}'`) where both 'field' and 'value' come directly from user-supplied request filters (POST body). Attackers can inject arbitrary SQL including subqueries and stacked statements.

searchGradeCorrectionNotes() concatenates user-controlled 'filters.noteContains' into raw SQL: `grade_history.note ILIKE '%${filters.noteContains}%'`. This is SQL injection. The 'courseId' parameter is also concatenated raw on line 1196.
listPartnerCatalogSorted() passes the user-controlled 'sortBy' query parameter directly to sql.raw(filters.sortBy) in the ORDER BY clause, allowing SQL injection via the ORDER BY expression.

convertCertificateToFormat() runs execSync(`pandoc ${sourcePath} -f html -t ${outputFormat} -o ${outputPath}`) where 'outputFormat' is user-controlled (from the certificate POST route body). Attacker-controlled values are interpolated into a shell command, enabling OS command injection.

exportEnrollmentTranscript() builds a shell command string `wkhtmltopdf --page-size ${preset} ${sourcePath} ${outputPath}` and runs it via exec(). 'preset' is user-controlled (from the transcript POST route body) and is not validated or escaped, allowing OS command injection.

loadAssignmentBriefTemplate() joins the user-controlled 'templateName' into a file path without basename() or traversal checks: path.join(ASSIGNMENT_BRIEF_TEMPLATES_DIR, templateName). The templateName comes from the appSettings value set via setAssignmentBriefTemplateAction, enabling arbitrary file read (path traversal).

loadSyllabusThemeStylesheet() builds the path join(SYLLABUS_THEMES_DIR, `${themeName}.css`) with the user-controlled 'themeName' (from the syllabus POST route body) and no traversal checks, allowing arbitrary file read via path traversal.

loadReportBrandingTemplate() joins the user-controlled 'reportType' (from the grades export query parameter) into path.join(REPORT_TEMPLATES_DIR, reportType) with no basename()/traversal check, enabling arbitrary file read.

saveCourseBannerImage() writes to path.join(COURSE_BANNERS_DIR, `${courseId}-${file.name}`) using the unvalidated uploaded file.name. A filename like '../../x' allows path traversal, writing arbitrary files outside the intended public/course-banners directory.

archiveGradeCorrectionRecord() writes to path.join(CASE_ARCHIVE_ROOT, `${caseLabel}.json`) where 'caseLabel' is user-controlled (the 'caseReference' form value in applyGradeCorrectionAction). Unlike archiveRosterAdjustmentRecord (which uses path.basename), this function does not sanitize the label, allowing path traversal file write.

searchPublishedCourseCatalog() interpolates the user-controlled 'codeQuery' directly into an XPath expression `/catalog/course[@code='${codeQuery}' ...]` without escaping (the escaping helper escapeXPathString is only used in the sibling widget function). This allows XPath injection to bypass the @status='published' filter and extract other catalog data.

resolvePartnerContentManifest() verifies JWTs with algorithms: ['HS256', 'none']. Accepting the 'none' algorithm allows attackers to forge an unsigned manifest token, bypassing signature verification and impersonating a partner district in the content-manifest exchange endpoint.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: resolveCostAllocationManifest() uses jwt.decode() which only decodes the token and performs NO signature verification. Anyone can forge an arbitrary cost-allocation manifest and it will be trusted by the cost-allocation endpoint, an authentication/authorization bypass.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: renderAssignmentInstructions() does NOT HTML-escape the input (unlike renderDiscussionBody which calls escapeHtml first). The result is rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML in assignments/[assignmentId]/page.tsx:32. Assignment instructions are stored and rendered as raw HTML, allowing stored XSS.

The 'continue_to' query parameter is passed unvalidated to NextResponse.redirect(). An attacker can craft a join link that redirects an authenticated user to an arbitrary external URL (open redirect / phishing). The sibling 'leave' route correctly whitelists destinations.

The 'exportLabel' query parameter is interpolated directly into the Content-Disposition header without CRLF stripping (unlike the sibling roster-summary route which sanitizes it). An attacker can inject CRLF to add arbitrary HTTP headers.

archiveCourseRecords() performs NO authentication or authorization check (no getCurrentUser() call). Any unauthenticated client can POST to this endpoint to archive a course and all of its assignments, a missing-authentication vulnerability. The sibling 'close' route properly checks auth.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: fetchExternalReadingPreview() fetches an arbitrary 'sourceUrl' supplied by the caller (reading-preview route) with no scheme/host validation. This allows server-side request forgery (SSRF) against internal network resources, including cloud metadata endpoints.

withPartnerCatalogHeaders() reflects the request's Origin header into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true for any origin. This allows any website to make credentialed cross-origin requests to this API-key-authenticated endpoint.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: Hardcoded fallback JWT signing secrets: EMBED_SIGNING_SECRET defaults to 'lms-embed-widget-secret' and GUARDIAN_SIGNING_SECRET to 'lms-guardian-link-secret'. If the environment variables are not set, tokens can be forged with these known secrets, defeating the embed/guardian link authentication.

Hardcoded fallback credentials: ALLOCATION_EXCHANGE_SECRET defaults to 'district-cost-allocation-secret' (line 5) and DISTRICT_SYNC_API_KEY defaults to 'district-sync-dev-key' (line 24). These known values allow forging billing reconciliation manifests and impersonating the sync service if the environment variables are unset.

createApiKeyAction() stores the raw API key in the 'keyHash' column (keyHash: rawKey) instead of a hash. The seeded key (seed.ts:471) correctly stores sha256(key). API keys are stored in cleartext, so a database compromise exposes usable credentials.

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

extra.message: importEnrollmentsAction() creates imported student accounts with a known default password 'ChangeMe!2026'. Any user who knows this default can authenticate as any imported student.
rotateWebhookSecretAction() generates the new webhook secret with Math.random().toString(36), a non-cryptographic PRNG, making the webhook HMAC secret predictable and forgeable.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: updateEnrollmentStatusAction() only checks that the actor is a school_admin or instructor, but never verifies the instructor is assigned to the enrollment's course (no getCourseScope/requireCourseAccess). Any instructor can change the enrollment status of any student in any course (IDOR / broken access control).

updateCohortScheduleAction() requires only the 'instructor' role and does not check that the actor is assigned to the cohort's course. Any instructor can update any cohort in the system, and the JSON 'patch' is spread into the update without field validation (mass assignment), enabling unauthorized changes to arbitrary cohorts.
